verdict.rationale: Superhuman documents a Cmd+K command palette that can 'instantly do any action' and teaches shortcuts. It also documents single-key navigation and snippet shortcuts, and a hands-on user confirms every interaction can be done from the keyboard. The 'never make me wait' speed claim is mixed: one user reports blazing-fast search and transitions, while an ex-user reports archive searches regularly taking ten seconds and occasional crashes requiring restarts, so the speed part of the story is not fully delivered. Missing for 10: consistent independent evidence of no-wait performance (search latency and crash reports contradict it), and a documented, comprehensive shortcut reference beyond blog mentions.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can do everything from the keyboard — comprehensive shortcuts and a command palette — in an interface fast enough to never make me wait

citations.quote: In Superhuman, one shortcut rules them all: Cmd+K. Cmd+K brings up Superhuman Command, where you can instantly do any action
where you can instantly do any action — and also learn the shortcut for next time
You can reply to important messages faster with blazingly fast shortcuts and features like Instant Intro.
To see your full calendar, just hit 2 or tap the calendar icon. (And hit 1 to jump back to your inbox.)
every interaction in Superhuman can be done from the keyboard, like an email version of vim
search and UI transitions are blazing fast
